editorial:
Imagine you are hanging out in New Orleans, but instead of jazz and food, you are dealing with a killer who literally cannot be killed. You follow a determined cop who is chasing a demonic monster that traded its soul to the devil for immortality. The whole vibe feels like a wild ride from the early nineties, mixing a police procedural with some supernatural weirdness. It is less about deep scares and more about the thrill of the hunt, making you feel like you are right there in the humid streets of Louisiana while this unstoppable force stalks its prey.

What really works here is the steady build-up and the cheesy but fun action scenes. The acting is decent for the time, though some of the special effects look a bit dated now. If you love old-school horror that does not take itself too seriously, you will have a blast.
endingExplained: In the end, the cop finally corners the immortal killer in a final showdown. Since bullets and knives do not work, the hero has to find a way to use the killer's own dark rules against him. After a brutal fight, the demon is finally defeated and sent back to hell. The movie wraps up with the city finally being safe, leaving you with the feeling that some evil things can actually be stopped.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves 90s horror and supernatural killers.
